en: From the "Chapter on the King of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s Vows" in the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya*:
Wandering through the lands of the ten directions throughout the three periods of time, O Lion among Men.
I leave none of those Buddhas behind; with body, speech, and mind purified, I prostrate to cultivate the power of the *Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna*.
As the Buddhas appear within the sphere of my thought, their bodies equal in measure to the atoms of all buddha-fields, I reverently pay homage to these Most Victorious Ones with a devout heart.
Upon a single atom are subtle atoms of Buddhas, Each surrounded by a host of Buddha-sons;
Thus it is throughout the entire Dharma-realm without exception— One should believe and understand that all Buddhas fill them.
The oceans of their virtues are inexhaustible when praised, And the ocean of their voices is a sea of wondrous sounds.
I praise the virtues of all Buddhas; I now extol all the Sugatas with the most excellent flowers and flower garlands, with bells, perfumes, and precious parasols,
with supreme lamps and incense— offering these to those Most Victorious Ones.
With various exquisite garments and incense, and supreme, variegated ornaments;
with heaps of sublime powdered incense as vast as Mount Sumeru— offering these to those most excellent ones,
the unsurpassed and magnanimous, one should offer them with faith to the most excellent.
Through the power of one who delights in practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra, I prostrate and make offerings to all the Most Victorious Ones.
Because I have been sustained by the forces of greed, hatred, and delusion, whatever transgressions I have committed through my physical, verbal, and mental actions,
I confess each and every one of them according to their respective categories.
Whatever merit has been cultivated by those most excellent in the ten directions, by the sons of the Buddha, by pratyekabuddhas, and by śrāvakas—
both those in training and those beyond training— I rejoice in all of it with my whole being.
Who among them shall become lamps for the world in the ten directions, gradually attaining enlightenment and realizing non-attachment?
To those teachers, I entreat them to turn the unsurpassed wheel;
To those who wish to enter parinirvāṇa, I entreat them for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings;
Or to remain in the world for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field— With palms joined, I shall make such entreaties.
I prostrate, make offerings, and confess; I entreat, rejoice, and inspire.
Whatever slight roots of merit I have accumulated, I dedicate them all toward enlightenment.
To all the Buddhas of the past throughout the ten directions—those who remain in the world and those who should be honored—I pay homage.
May all the World-Honored Ones of the future realize perfect enlightenment swiftly;
may all the lands throughout the ten directions become vast and pure;
and may all the sons of the Buddhas reach fulfillment at the foot of the Bodhi tree.
May all classes of sentient beings throughout the ten directions be free from the suffering of illness and always abide in peace and happiness;
may the meaning of all dharmas possessed by these beings be realized, and may they together achieve the practice of Bodhi.
As I cultivate this practice, may I know my past lives in every place where I am born.
In life after life, through the succession of bodies, may I always dwell in places where the Buddhas appear;
may I rely upon the most excellent teachings and practice them with diligence.
May my conduct as Samantabhadra be perfected, and may my observance of the precepts be stainless and utterly pure; may I uphold them forever without flaw or deficiency.
To devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and kumbhāṇḍas, to humans and non-humans, and all such classes—
according to their various voices and sounds, I shall preach the Dharma for them all.
May they cultivate the perfections with purity, goodness, and diligence, and may they never forget the bodhicitta.
May all those who have committed offenses through various banners be completely extinguished without remainder;
may they be liberated from karma and the paths of Māra, wandering freely through the world,
unattached like a lotus in water, and practicing without hindrance like the sun and moon.
Throughout all lands and every direction, may the manifold sufferings of the evil realms be eliminated;

may all sentient beings be established in peace and happiness. To benefit the various classes of beings throughout the realms and to bring the cultivation of bodhi to fulfillment, may I enter into the midst of the diverse conducts of all living beings.
Revealing all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, I shall practice them throughout all future kalpas.
Who could possibly match me in performing these deeds?
May I always be in accord with them in body, speech, and mind, And become one with their practiced vows.
May I always meet those virtuous friends who delight in benefiting me and who reveal the practices and vows of Samantabhadra,
and may I never harbor thoughts of opposition toward them.
May I constantly behold before my eyes those teachers of the path who bestow grace upon the children of the Buddha.
One should perform great offerings there, never wearying throughout all future kalpas,
to protect and uphold the supreme and wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas; showing the way for those who practice toward enlightenment,
if one purifies the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, one should practice it throughout all future kalpas.

While revolving through all states of existence, may I obtain inexhaustible merit and wisdom, as well as concentration, wisdom, skillful means, and all liberations; may I become an inexhaustible treasury of virtues.
Upon a single mote of dust, there are subtle-dust realms, and in those realms, there are boundless Buddhas, infinite in number.
Surrounded by a host of Buddha-sons in the center, one should gaze upon those who practice the conduct of enlightenment.
Thus, throughout these inexhaustible directions, within the tip of a single hair,
one should enter the ocean of Buddhas and the ocean of lands across the three periods of time, as well as the essential practices cultivated throughout oceans of eons.
With a single word and sound, they branch out into an ocean of all languages; These are the branches of the pure speech of all Buddhas, which,

according to the inclinations of beings in their various realms, Constantly cause them to enter the resonance of the Buddha’s voice and to roam among the most supreme ones of the three times, Turning the wheel of Dharma for all in accordance with the truth.
I should enter those inexhaustible voices of all the Buddhas through the power of wisdom;
if I were to enter them throughout the duration of future eons, I would do so in a single instant.
Who, having measured the equality of the eons of the three times, would not practice by entering into each according to that very instant?
Those who roam through the three times as lions among men—may I behold them at every moment.
May I always enter into their sphere of activity, which is liberated like an illusion.
Who is it that adorns the lands of the three times and establishes them all upon a single atom?
Thus, throughout all these inexhaustible directions, I shall go to where all those future lamps of the world enter into the adornments of the Buddha-fields,
where they shall attain the state of a fully awakened one, turn the wheel of Dharma, manifest parinirvāṇa,
and proceed to the limit of reality— all those guides to whom I ought to go.
Pervading all powers of swift supernatural faculties, Pervading all powers of the various vehicles through the universal gate,
Pervading all powers of merit from various practices, Pervading all powers of universal compassion and equanimity,
Pervading all powers of merit from every goodness, The power of great wisdom accomplished by the unattached.
The power of wisdom, skillful means, concentration, and insight; The power of truly accomplishing bodhi;
The power that can most purely purify all karma; The power that destroys all suffering and affliction;
The power that subdues all māras; The power of fulfilling the practices of Samantabhadra.
May all oceans of lands be purified; May all oceans of sentient beings be liberated;
May all oceans of dharmas be perceived; May all oceans of wisdom be contemplated;
May all oceans of conduct be purified; And may all oceans of vows be fulfilled.
I shall offer worship to the oceans of all Buddhas, the Worthy Ones; Throughout oceans of eons, I shall practice without weariness.

Whoever wanders through the three times among the most supreme ones, And cultivates the various distinctions of the practices and vows for enlightenment— Having attained equal awakening through the conduct of Samantabhadra, May I fulfill them all completely, without exception.
Among all the sons of the Buddhas, he possesses the most majestic power; therefore, he is named Samantabhadra.
Those wise ones who are able to practice those deeds together should dedicate all these virtues:
may their bodily, verbal, and mental actions be pure; may all their practices be purified and all buddha-fields be purified.
How may I fully dedicate like Samantabhadra? May I likewise practice those deeds;
because all practices are the conduct of Samantabhadra, I shall also practice the conduct of Mañjuśrī, Until the end of the future eons, never wearying;
May all that he has accomplished be brought to fulfillment.
May the practices they cultivate be immeasurable, and may their merits likewise be boundless;
though they abide in these infinite and supreme deeds,
their miraculous transformations should be known to extend to the very limits of space, and the limitlessness of sentient beings is likewise so.
The limit of all karma and the limit of afflictions—may the measure of my own vows be likewise.
May these infinite lands of the ten directions be adorned with jewels and offered to the Buddhas, as well as to humans and the assembly of noble ones, along with exquisite music;
may I maintain such offerings through kalpas as numerous as the atoms of those lands.
Whoever hears this Sūtra on Dedication And gives rise to faith and understanding toward supreme enlightenment,
If they can produce even a single moment of faith in this, They will immediately become a mass of most excellent merit.
Whoever gives rise to these practices and vows of Samantabhadra Shall thereby abandon all evil destinies.
They are also called those who have distanced themselves from all evil friends; such people will swiftly behold Amitābha.
These individuals shall obtain the most supreme peace and longevity, and in this present life, they shall also summon every wish-fulfilling joy.
Just as with Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, so too shall these [practitioners] become before long.
Whoever, driven by the power of ignorance, Has committed the five crimes of immediate retribution and other such sins,
If they can recite this conduct of Samantabhadra, It will be swiftly extinguished without remainder.
Their wisdom will be majestic, endowed with all the marks of excellence, And their lineage and the *ūrṇā-kośa* will be perfectly complete.
Just as no Māras or non-Buddhists can equal you, All those within the three realms offer you worship;
Swiftly proceed to the Bodhi tree of sovereign enlightenment, And for the benefit of sentient beings,
sit there to attain perfect awakening and turn the wheel of Dharma, Subduing all the hosts of Māra’s armies.
Whoever upholds, recites, and expounds these practices and vows of Samantabhadra—their fruit and retribution is known only to the Buddha;
have no doubt regarding supreme enlightenment.
Mañjuśrī, the Heroic and Mighty One, and all that is to be known, as well as the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, are likewise so.
I practice according to that model; all these virtues I dedicate.
To those who wander through the three times, the most excellent of all; among all dedications, the supreme one:
by means of these roots of virtue, I dedicate them for the sake of practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra.
When I am on the verge of passing away, may all veils and hindrances be dispelled;
may I behold Amitābha Buddha directly before me, swiftly depart for the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and reach that realm.
May all such practices and vows manifest clearly and completely before me.
Thus may I be perfectly complete without exception, benefiting all sentient beings throughout the world;
in that most exquisite and wondrous Buddha-field of Sukhāvatī, may I be born within a sublime lotus flower and,
in the presence of the Most Excellent Amitābha, may I receive the prediction of my future enlightenment.
Having received that prediction from him, I attained immeasurable billions of supernormal powers;
by the power of wisdom, I pervade the ten directions and extensively benefit all sentient beings.
—From the "Chapter on the King of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s Vows and Practices" in the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Great Vaipulya Scripture.
